stem:
Sana leaves a bowl of plain cooked rice uncovered on a warm kitchen shelf. She also keeps a jar of lemon pickle and a jar of murabba made with enough salt or sugar.

Which claims correctly explain the difference? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Microorganisms from the surroundings can settle on the uncovered rice and spoil it.
Enough salt or sugar in the pickle and murabba stops microorganisms from infecting them in the same way.
Even a tiny pinch of salt or sugar is enough to stop microorganisms from infecting any food.
The rice spoils first, and that spoiling then produces the microorganisms.

teacher.key_rationale: Microorganisms are widespread and can infect exposed food; high salt or sugar concentrations preserve pickle and murabba.
